props.gloss_en: Rav Chisda: one walking on the road who found an animal whose mouth was mutilated inspects its hooves: if they are cloven it is known to be kosher; if not, non-kosher
Rav Chisda: provided he recognizes a pig

the school of R' Yishmael: 'the pig, for it parts the hoof' (Lev 11:7) -- the Ruler of His world knows there is nothing that parts the hoof and is non-kosher but the pig; therefore the verse specified it with 'it'

Rav Chisda: one walking in the wilderness who found an animal whose mouth was mutilated and whose hooves were cut inspects its flesh: if it runs warp and woof it is known to be kosher; if not, non-kosher
Rav Chisda: provided he recognizes the arvad
and where does he inspect [the flesh]? at the wings of the tailbone

supports.gloss_en: דתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל -- 'it': only the pig parts the hoof and is non-kosher, so no other species defeats the hoof inspection

objections.gloss_en: לאו אמרת איכא חזיר? איכא נמי מינא אחרינא דדמיא לחזיר! -- perhaps another species resembles the pig

answered_by.gloss_en: גמירי דליכא -- it is learned by tradition that there is none
